title: JavaScript Promises Core Check
description: Check your understanding of Promise states, creation, then/catch/finally, chaining, combinators, promisifying callbacks, and timeout patterns.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A future result of asynchronous work

questions.explanation: A Promise represents async work that may fulfill or reject later.

questions.prompt: Which are the main Promise states?
questions.explanation: A Promise starts pending and later settles as fulfilled or rejected.

questions.prompt: What does `resolve(value)` do inside a Promise executor?
questions.explanation: `resolve(value)` fulfills the Promise with the provided value.

questions.prompt: What does `reject(error)` do inside a Promise executor?

options.text: Rejects the Promise with a reason
Turns the Promise into an array

questions.explanation: `reject(error)` rejects the Promise, usually with an Error object.

questions.prompt: Which method handles a fulfilled Promise value?
Which method handles a rejected Promise?

questions.explanation: `.finally()` is for cleanup that should happen whether the Promise succeeds or fails.

questions.prompt: What should you usually do in a `.then()` callback when the next step depends on another Promise?
questions.explanation: Returning the Promise makes the chain wait and passes its result to the next `.then()`.

questions.prompt: Which combinator rejects if any input Promise rejects?
questions.explanation: `Promise.all()` fulfills only if all inputs fulfill and rejects if any input rejects.

questions.prompt: Which combinator gives you every outcome, including rejections?
questions.explanation: `Promise.allSettled()` waits for all inputs and returns fulfilled/rejected outcome objects.

options.text: Converting a callback-based API into a Promise-based API

questions.explanation: Promisifying wraps callback APIs so they can be used with promises or async/await.

questions.prompt: Does `Promise.race()` automatically cancel promises that lose the race?
questions.explanation: `Promise.race()` settles with the first settled Promise but does not automatically cancel other operations.
